discoveries: (1) In this sandbox `uv pip freeze` fails with exit 2, "Could not acquire lock … Read-only file system" on `~/.cache/uv`. A launched session's doctor will therefore never read the reranker venv's freeze hash and falls back to reading package versions; my loaded runs gave uv a temporary cache. (2) The non-UTF-8 decode route in `_git` is reached only with `core.quotePath false`; with git's default the name comes back quoted and nothing fails. (3) `gov status`'s `_doctor` re-raises a GovError without `healthy` in its details, so its `_part` now shows the DOCTOR_PART_FAILED text as the reason doctor was not read.
risks: A rulesync call that never answers now holds the check 25 s, not 10, and up to 50 s when `--version` is slow and `generate` hangs. That is still inside the 60 s, but only 10 s are left if the runner's default or the check's own work grows. The new unit case fails if the runner's limit drops. The timeout finding keeps the code RULESYNC_FAILED and is told apart only by its message "no answer within 25 seconds" (W2-57's and W1-38's suites pass with it). `gov doctor` can take up to about 100 s when tools hang.
lessons: `git commit -- <path>` does not take an untracked file: `git add -- <path>` first. Measuring beside W1-38 alone reached only load 6; close-like load (about 48) needed several suites at `-n 40`. The measurement script runs its load in its own process group and kills that group at a deadline, so nothing is left running.
